newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour's Brown to announce business "summit".
newsitem.headline: UK Labour's Brown to announce business "summit".

text.p: The Labour party is to drive home its bid for the support of Britain's entrepreneurs on Friday with the promise of a "business manifesto".
Labour economics spokesman Gordon Brown will also announce a February "summit" bringing together businessmen from across the country and senior members of the opposition party, aides said.

The speech is one of a series designed to fill out the details of Labour's economic policies before the election which Prime Minister John Major must call by May at the latest. Polls make Labour favourites for the election.
But the government is fighting desperately to cut Labour's lead, arguing that its policies have created the best economic conditions Britain has seen in decades.
But the polls and records of political donations show that business is warming to Labour as it gets closer to power.
This has been encouraged by Brown and Labour leader Tony Blair, who are determined to show the party has ditched its old "tax-and-spend" instincts and is committed to a market economy.
Aides said Brown would announce that Labour's business manifesto will be sent to 10,000 companies and chambers of commerce across Britain.
